references.text: The Israelites are God's servants whom he brought out of Egypt; therefore they cannot be sold as slaves.
God identifies himself as the one who brought the Israelites out of Egypt and declares himself their Lord.
God presents himself as the Lord who brought Israel out of Egypt, the basis of his authority over the people.
A reminder that the Lord brought the people out of Egypt from slavery.
God declares that Israel belongs to him; he has created and formed them.
Believers are freed from sin and have become God's servants, paralleling Israel's deliverance from Egypt.
Believers belong to God because they were bought with a price, and should honor God with their bodies.
The one called in the Lord is the Lord's freed person, bought at a price, and must not become slaves of men.
Believers are redeemed by Christ's precious blood, not with perishable things.
